task: An epidemic is spreading through major cities, killing 5–10% of the population per month. Coordinate an immediate public-health response within your governance structure.

dispatches.responsibility: Draft and issue the imperial emergency edict declaring epidemic status, ordering city cordons, releasing treasury funds, and convening the response; specify reporting cadence to the throne.
Remonstrate on the draft edict, ensure legal and ritual propriety, verify ministerial mandates are within their lawful remit, and seal the edict before promulgation.

Coordinate the six ministries as the executive hub, hold daily briefings at the Du Zheng Hall, integrate reports from each ministry, and escalate unresolved conflicts or shortages directly to the Emperor.
Mobilize and dispatch Imperial Medical Bureau physicians, apothecaries, and quarantine officers to affected cities; appoint regional Epidemic Response Commissioners; rotate staff to prevent burnout.
Open the emergency treasury, allocate silver and grain from state granaries, fix prices on medicine and food, remit taxes in stricken prefectures, and publish daily expenditure ledgers.

Construct isolation wards, plague hospitals, mass crematoria, and sanitary infrastructure; requisition workshops to produce medicine, masks, and herbal decoctions; repair roads for medical supply convoys.
Deploy garrison troops to enforce cordons on infected cities, escort medicine convoys, prevent panic flight, secure granaries against hoarding, and assist in contact tracing and burial squads.

Enforce the emergency epidemic code — prosecute rumor-mongers, medicine hoarders, and quarantine violators; investigate graft in relief disbursement; handle succession and property disputes for the deceased.
